afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 081128
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
428 AM MST Tue Sep 8 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Above normal temperatures will prevail through the rest of the 
 work week, resulting in widespread Moderate Heat Risk and areas 
 of Major Heat Risk.

- Extreme Heat Warnings will be in effect for portions of the 
  lower deserts through the end of the work week.

- Thunderstorm coverage is expected to increase during the latter
  half of the week across Eastern and Central Arizona, with 
  slight chances becoming introduced for the South Central Arizona
  lower deserts by Thursday.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Southwesterly flow aloft is still apparent in midlevel water 
vapor imagery, as the region is sandwiched between troughing over 
a good chunk of the Western US and expansive ridging centered over
the Southern Plains and Mississippi River Valley region. Mid and 
high level clouds continue to stream northeastward over the area, 
with some areas of embedded virga showers/sprinkles registering 
on early morning MRMS composite reflectivity. These will likely 
continue through the early morning hours until the influence of 
the southwesterly flow aloft diminishes. The forecast remains 
largely on track, with a pattern shift occurring by the middle of 
the week. Troughing over the Western US is shown retreating to the
north, allowing the subtropical high to retrograde westward and 
settle almost directly overhead Wednesday. During this time, the 
subtropical high will quickly strengthen with H5 heights aloft 
briefly peaking near climatological maximum values for this time 
of year, around 596-597 dam. NAEFS/ENS mean 850 mb temperatures 
between the 80th-95th percentiles of climatology, around 26C-30C 
over the forecast area, will support afternoon highs around 5F 
above daily normals. Periods of mid to high clouds have been 
maintained overnight due to the continued southwesterly flow and 
are expected the next few nights due to decaying or distant 
upstream convective activity over Sonora/Southeastern AZ, which 
will prevent more efficient radiative cooling. Thus, morning lows 
are forecast to attain a 7F-10F above normal range, offering 
little relief from the daytime heat. These temperatures will 
translate to widespread Moderate HeatRisk with areas of Major 
HeatRisk across the typically hotter lower desert locales. As a 
result, Extreme Heat Warnings go into effect later this morning 
for the Phoenix Metro, portions of South-Central and Southwest AZ 
including the Yuma area, and portions of Imperial County including
the Imperial Valley. Extreme Heat Warnings expand slightly 
further north Wednesday along the Lower CO River Valley and 
surrounding communities. 

With the pattern change occurring by the middle of the week, flow
aloft will shift southeasterly, and daily gulf surges are 
expected to reestablish. These factors will combine with vigorous 
upstream convection over Sonora to help push abundant low level 
moisture into the area, especially by Wednesday night. Mixing 
ratios will surge back above 10-12 g/kg across South-Central and 
even Southwest AZ, supportive of lower desert storms if there is a
sufficient lifting mechanism. However, anticyclonic subsidence 
centered nearly directly overhead will act to suppress deep moist 
convection except over prominent terrain features of Southeastern 
and Eastern AZ through Wednesday. Latest HREF does indicate the 
potential for spotty elevated showers to develop tonight across 
portions of the forecast area, but this is likely conditional on 
sufficiently strong gravity waves propagating north and west from 
earlier strong storm clusters over Sonora. 

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...    
Late this week is shaping up to be a more active period for 
monsoon thunderstorms across at least South-Central AZ. By 
Thursday, anticyclonic subsidence will begin to diminish as the 
subtropical high weakens overhead, and abundant low level moisture
will remain in place through the rest of the week and linger into
the weekend. Latest NBM guidance seems to favor Friday with the 
best chances for lower desert thunderstorms, which makes sense 
given the weaker subsidence aloft and plenty of moisture and 
instability to support numerous thunderstorms over the high 
terrain by the afternoon, sending outflows into the lower deserts 
and triggering additional thunderstorms by the evening. GFS bufr 
soundings indicate a good balance between CAPE and DCAPE Thursday 
evening, with values between 1000-1500 J/kg, which is typically a 
good indicator for severe weather potential over the Valley. 
However, CIN may be a bit stronger than preferred, and the 
development of thunderstorms that can utilize this environment 
will be entirely dependent on the presence and timing of a 
sufficient lifting mechanism (i.e., thunderstorm outflow 
boundary). This conditional threat continues Friday, but with 
perhaps lower DCAPE and shallower inverted-V soundings. Strong 
thunderstorm winds, dense blowing dust, locally heavy rainfall 
resulting in instances of flash flooding, and frequent lightning 
will all be on the table for thunderstorm hazards later this week.

The forecast for this weekend into early next week is much less 
certain, however, a few more details are coming into focus tonight
compared to the guidance available in previous forecast updates. 
Ensembles are in better agreement that mean troughing will 
establish over the Northwest US, pushing the northern stream and 
likely a series of upper lows and their attendant jet streaks as 
far south as the Great Basin. WPC cluster analysis reveals 
discrepancies on how far south the mean troughing will establish 
and how strongly negative the midlevel height anomalies will 
become over the Northwest US. The current consensus is for flow 
aloft to shift south to southwesterly as a result, meaning the 
more typical monsoonal pattern which briefly sets up this week 
will be short-lived, becoming something more akin to a transition 
season setup. This does not, however, mean that thunderstorm 
chances leave the forecast. Drying will begin to occur from west 
to east, but low level moisture will not be scoured out from 
Southern AZ. Thunderstorms will likely continue to favor 
development over prominent terrain features, and lower desert 
storm chances will be dependent on outflows or a nearly uncapped 
environment. As for now, NBM/WPC PoPs have come in lower this 
weekend compared to Thu/Fri, and timing of the better chances 
seems a bit unrealistic, reflecting the high uncertainty and 
nebulous forcing mechanisms. Regardless, the main message for this
weekend into early next week will be continued thunderstorm 
chances over at least South-Central AZ higher terrain areas, but 
likely a decrease in activity from Thu/Fri due to the pattern 
shift and until southeasterly flow returns. 

With the subtropical high diminished and then displaced by 
Northwest US troughing this weekend, temperatures will follow a 
downward trend, attaining near normal values likely by Saturday or
Sunday, ending the extreme heat conditions.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1125Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No significant weather issues will exist through tonight under
periodic mid/high cigs. Light east winds for the rest of the
morning will turn back to the west around noon with limited
afternoon/early evening gusts.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No weather issues will exist through tonight under occasional 
mid/high cigs. Winds will generally favor a W/NW heading through 
the afternoon before switching to a southerly direction. Periods 
of nearly calm conditions will also be common. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Above normal temperatures will prevail through the end of the work
week, then temperatures are likely to decrease closer to normal 
over the weekend. Afternoon minimum humidities will generally 
range between 18-30% areawide through much of the week following
fair to good overnight recoveries between 35-70%. Fairly typical 
diurnal winds with occasional afternoon upslope breeziness can be 
expected through Thursday, followed by an increase in southerly to
southwesterly winds Friday into this weekend. Rain and 
thunderstorm chances will remain low and mostly limited to the 
eastern Arizona high terrain through midweek before slight chances
become introduced to the lower deserts of at least the eastern 
districts during the latter half of the week.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM this morning to 8 PM MST 
     Thursday for AZZ531-532-535>544-546-548>551-559.

     Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM Wednesday to 8 PM MST Friday for 
     AZZ530-533.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM this morning to 8 PM PDT Friday 
     for CAZ562-566-567.

     Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM Wednesday to 8 PM PDT Friday for 
     CAZ569-570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Whittock
LONG TERM...Whittock
AVIATION...18/Kuhlman
FIRE WEATHER...Whittock
